findings.title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM).
findings.comment: Observed that the only CFPM on staff was not present today. The General Manager is working on renewing their CFPM. Ensure that a Certified Food Protection Manager is present at all times of when food preparation is happening.
findings.citation_text: 2-102.12(A) Certified Food Protection Manager. (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM. [C]

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
findings.comment: 1ST REPEAT: Observed that the handwashing sink in the bar was obstructed by a drink pitcher, and was out of paper towels and soap. CORRECTED: Staff were notified, the pitcher was removed from the handwashing sink, and the paper towels and soap were refilled. Ensure that handwashing sinks are not used for purposes other than handwashing, are fully accessible for handwashing at all times, and are fully stocked with soap and paper towels.
findings.citation_text: 5-205.11 Using a Handwashing Sink. (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for EMPLOYEE use. (B) A HANDWASHING SINK may not be used for purposes other than handwashing. (C) An automatic handwashing facility shall be used in accordance with manufacturer’s instructions. [Pf]

findings.title: Food separated and protected.
findings.comment: Observed that liquid eggs were stored above RTE foods like yogurt and strawberries in the front area 2-door cooler. CORRECTED: Inspector discussed with Staff, and eggs were moved below RTE foods. Inspector and Staff further discussed that items with different cooking temperatures can be stored side-by-side as long as they are not in contact with each other. Ensure that raw animal proteins are stored below RTE foods that do not require cooking to be eaten.
findings.citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(1) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (1) Except as specified in (1)(d) below or when combined as ingredients, separating raw animal FOODS during storage, preparation, holding, and display from: (a) Raw READY-TO-EAT FOOD including other raw animal FOOD such as FISH for sushi or MOLLUSCAN SHELLFISH, or other raw READY-TOEAT FOOD such as fruits and vegetables, (b) Cooked READY-TO-EAT FOOD, and (c) Fruits and vegetables before they are washed; (d) Frozen, commercially processed and packaged raw animal FOOD may be stored or displayed with or above frozen, commercially processed and packaged, ready-to-eat food. [P]

findings.title: Food separated and protected.
findings.comment: Observed that carafes of juice were being cold held in the service ice that is used for drinks. CORRECTED: Inspector educated staff that ice used for beverages (“eating ice” or “service ice”) is not to be used for a secondary purpose like cold holding beverages, as there is a strong potential for cross-contamination from both the exterior of the containers and from spills. Staff removed the containers from the service ice, and will cease this practice. Inspector discussed if Staff want to keep additional juices cold, they should use a separate cooler or a separate ice bath where the ice inside is only used for cooling. Ensure that service ice is only used for ice inside of beverages, and not for cooling food. [P]

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: Observed that the sanitizer bucket in the front part of the kitchen did not measure any concentration of quaternary ammonium sanitizer (0ppm). Sanitizing solution was hot to the touch. CORRECTED: Inspector asked Staff if the sanitizing solution was sourced from the triple sink hose, and it was. The triple sink’s bottle of sanitizer is not empty. Staff made the sanitizing solution how it had been made that morning, with hot water, and the sanitizing solution again read 0ppm. Inspector educated Staff that quaternary ammonium sanitizing solution should be made with water that is 75 F (room temperature). Staff remade the sanitizing solution, this time just using cold water. The sanitizing solution measured at 200ppm for quaternary ammonium. Ensure that chemical sanitizing solution of quaternary ammonium is used per manufacturer’s guidelines for temperature and chemical concentration: room temperature water (65-75 F) and a concentration that is effective for sanitizing, 200-400ppm.
findings.citation_text: 4-501.114(C) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (C) A quaternary ammonium compound solution shall: (1) Have a minimum temperature of 24°C (75°F), (2) Have a concentration as specified under § 7-204.11 and as indicated by the manufacturer's use directions included in the labeling, and (3) Be used only in water with 500 MG/L hardness or less or in water having a hardness no greater than specified by the EPA-registered label use instructions. [P]

findings.title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used.
findings.comment:
3RD REPEAT: Observed the stainless steel shelf above the three compartment sink is rusted above and below. The shelf must either be replaced or painted and sealed. Ensure that the shelf is a smooth, easily cleanable surface by the next routine inspection. NOTE that fixing the ventilation in that area (violation #56: non-working heat dish machine ventilation hood) may prevent additional rusting in the area.

4-101.11(B)-(E) Characteristics. Materials that are used in the construction of UTENSILS and FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT may not allow the migration of deleterious substances or impart colors, odors, or tastes to FOOD and under normal use conditions shall be: (B) Durable, CORROSION-RESISTANT, and nonabsorbent; (C) Sufficient in weight and thickness to withstand repeated WAREWASHING; (D) Finished to have a SMOOTH, EASILY CLEANABLE surface; and (E) Resistant to pitting, chipping, crazing, scratching, scoring, distortion, and decomposition. [C]

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
findings.comment:
Observed the following non-food contact surfaces require cleaning:
(i) there is an accumulation of ice in the walk-in freezer. A tray that has been placed to catch the drips, but the ice is no longer contained in the tray, and is starting to fall on boxes.
(ii) many handles in the kitchen are sticky to the touch (hot box handles, the sauce cooler).
(iii) there is an accumulation of soil residues on the fans and the ceiling in the walk-in cooler.
Non-food contact surfaces must be cleaned at a frequency necessary to avoid the accumulation of dust, dirt, food residue, grease, and other debris. Ensure that the above referenced are cleaned to sight and touch by the next routine inspection.
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris. [C]

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment:
Inspectors observed the following areas that are in need of repair:
(i) FIRST REPEAT: the baseboards on the floor between and next to the walk-in cooler and freezer.
(ii) FIRST REPEAT: the walk-in cooler and freezer doors are difficult to shut and open - there is an accumulation of ice / water at the bottom areas.
(iii) the handwashing sink near the dish area has water pressure issues that is causing the water to spray everywhere.
The PIC was informed, and made plans for repair by the next routine inspection. Ensure that equipment and physical facilities are in a state of good repair.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair. [C]

findings.title: Adequate ventilation and lighting; designated areas used.
findings.comment: 1ST REPEAT: Observed that the ventilation hood over the heat dish machine was not working, causing an excess of condensation in the surrounding area, including the ceiling HVAC vent (observed to be rusted), and excessive steam pushing out into the surrounding area. Steam rises up, pools in the ventilation hood, then bounces back down and out into the kitchen instead of sucked up by the ventilation. This could be contributing to the rusted shelving observed in the kitchen area as well. The PIC was informed, and made plans for its repair by the next routine inspection. Ensure that ventilation hood systems are sufficient in capacity to prevent condensation from collecting.
findings.citation_text: 4-301.14 Ventilation Hood Systems, Adequacy. Ventilation hood systems and devices shall be sufficient in number and capacity to prevent grease or condensation from collecting on walls and ceilings. [C]

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: Inspectors observed an ice scoop with an accumulation of debris in the clean drying shelves. CORRECTED: The PIC was informed and the scoop was put in the dish machine. Ensure that food-contact surfaces and utensil are clean to sight and touch.
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures.
findings.comment: Inspectors observed that the large standing cooler for the establishment’s bulk dressings and sauces was not cooling sufficiently - sauces were probed at a temperature of 45°F. The PIC was informed, and the cooler was set to a colder temperature. CORRECTED: TCS foods were moved to the walk-in cooler for the time being, and the PIC will monitor the temperature of the standing cooler to see if it is adequate for cooling going forward. Ensure that the cooler is functioning properly - cold holding below 41°F - before returning TCS foods to it.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(2) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained:(2) At 5°C (41°F) or less.

findings.comment:
Observed the following non-food contact surfaces require cleaning:

(1) The grease on the floor and on the side of the fryer and oven. 

(2) The food debris on the gaskets of the freezer by the fryers. 

(3) The dust behind the juice machine nozzles.

(4) The debris on the bottom of the ice scoop holder at the bar. 

(5) The dust and other debris on the shelf holding milk and creamer in the walk-in cooler. 

(6) The debris on the bottom of the black containers holding clean dishes next to the walk-in freezer.
